First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{2x} & ={10}^{x-7} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{x-7})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)=(x-7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =(x-7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) & =-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x & =\frac{7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$
